recentItems.title: Iran hits US bases and civilian sites in the Gulf after a lull | Inside Story
recentItems.description:
After months of lull, Iran is again striking US assets in Gulf countries again. 
Civilian facilities have been damaged. 
Is Iran just tightening its grip on the world's economy? Can Tehran force the White House to ease its economic blockade?
And could this revive a full-scale conflict? 

Presenter: Rob Matheson

Guests:
Ali Akbar Dareini -- Researcher at the Center for Strategic Studies

Barbara Slavin -- Distinguished Fellow at the Stimson Center

Mehran Kamrava -- Professor of Government at Georgetown University in Qatar

recentItems.title: Israeli attacks on Palestinian paramedics surge in occupied West Bank
recentItems.description:
Across Gaza and the occupied West Bank, Palestinian paramedics face an increase in Israeli settler attacks and military restrictions, putting patients’ lives at risk.
A new report reveals how fear and obstruction are preventing health workers from reaching those in need.

Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim reports from Silwad in the occupied West Bank.

recentItems.title: Why did COP31 climate talks collapse without a deal?
recentItems.description:
The longest UN climate summit in history collapsed without a final deal in Turkiye, the first such failure in 17 years. With countries divided over fossil fuels and climate finance, Al Jazeera’s Mikail Malik spoke to campaigners and negotiators about who was responsible.

recentItems.title: As Iceland melts, a former PM calls for action | Talk to Al Jazeera
recentItems.description:
Iceland's former prime minister says that although climate change has fallen lower down on the international political agenda, it remains an existential crisis.

Katrin Jakobsdottir says our warming world is not just a catastrophe for nature, but a health and security emergency that cannot be ignored.

Her country is on the front lines of that emergency, with the Arctic warming at four times the rate of the rest of the world.

Almost all of Iceland's glaciers are rapidly retreating - one was declared "dead" in 2019.

Jakobsdottir says it all comes at a time when the world's biggest powers are flexing their muscles - and the politics of compromise are being squeezed out.

recentItems.title: Rescue teams search rubble after deadly Russian attack near Kyiv | AJ #shorts
recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after unanimous board vote
recentItems.description:
The US tech giant Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO.
He stepped down earlier this month after admitting he had a relationship with a woman who was alleged to be Chinese spy.
The company's stock has skyrocketed in response to the news, climbing about 30 percent in early trading.

Al Jazeera's Richard Gaisford reports from Washington, DC.

recentItems.title: US Army plans to detonate explosives in Iowa as residents fear lead exposure
recentItems.description:

People living near the ammunition plant fear the blast could expose them to toxic lead. 

Al Jazeera’s Julide Ayger reports.
